flashcards.q: What is the scaled dot-product attention formula?
flashcards.a: softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V -- Q and K scored via dot product, scaled by 1/sqrt(d_k), softmaxed into weights, then used to weight-average V.

flashcards.q: Derive why attention scores are divided by sqrt(d_k), not d_k or nothing.
flashcards.a: If Q,K components are iid mean-0 variance-1, the dot product over d_k terms has variance d_k (sum of d_k independent unit-variance products), so std dev grows as sqrt(d_k). Dividing by sqrt(d_k) restores unit variance regardless of d_k; dividing by d_k over-shrinks variance below 1 and pushes softmax toward uniform.

flashcards.q: What happens if attention scores are not scaled at large d_k?
flashcards.a: Large-variance scores saturate softmax toward one-hot output, and softmax's own gradient factor softmax_i(1-softmax_i) collapses toward zero almost everywhere, stalling gradient flow.

flashcards.q: What is the time and memory cost of naive self-attention, and which one is the practical bottleneck?
flashcards.a: O(n^2 d_k) time, O(n^2) memory per head (the QK^T matrix). Memory is the practical limiter -- at n=8192 fp16, one head's score matrix is ~128MB.

flashcards.q: What is the KV cache size formula per token?
flashcards.a: 2 * n_kv_heads * d_head * bytes_per_element (the 2 accounts for storing both K and V).

flashcards.q: How does MQA reduce KV cache size versus MHA?
flashcards.a: MQA (Shazeer, 2019) shares one KV head across all query heads, dividing KV cache size by h (the number of query heads), at a measurable quality cost on summarization and long-context retrieval.

flashcards.q: How does GQA reduce KV cache size versus MHA, and what config does Llama-family 70B use?
flashcards.a: GQA (Ainslie et al., 2023) groups query heads into g groups sharing one KV head each, dividing cache by h/g. Llama-family 70B uses 64 query heads over 8 KV heads -- an 8x reduction, recovering nearly all MHA quality.

flashcards.q: What is Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and how does it differ from GQA?
flashcards.a: MLA (DeepSeek-V2/V3) compresses K and V into a shared low-rank latent vector via learned projections rather than sharing discrete heads. GQA reduces the COUNT of KV heads; MLA reduces the DIMENSIONALITY stored per cached position. DeepSeek-V3 reports ~70KB/token vs 192-328KB/token for comparable GQA models.

flashcards.q: What is the worked KV-cache example for a 70B model (80 layers, GQA-8, head_dim=128, BF16) at 4k and 128k context?
flashcards.a: 0.32 MB/token (2*80*8*128*2 bytes). At 4,096 tokens: ~1.3GB per sequence. At 128,000 tokens: ~42GB per sequence -- larger than many single GPUs' total VRAM.

flashcards.q: Why is FlashAttention described as exact rather than approximate?
flashcards.a: It computes the mathematically identical softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V output -- it changes memory access order (tiling + online/running softmax), not what is computed. Approximate methods (Linformer, sparse attention) change the computed function itself.

flashcards.q: Does FlashAttention change the asymptotic time complexity of attention?
flashcards.a: No -- it stays O(n^2) time (same FLOP count). It changes memory from O(n^2) to O(n) by never materializing the full score matrix in HBM, and improves constant-factor speed via better hardware utilization.

flashcards.q: What are FlashAttention-3's reported speedups on H100?
flashcards.a: 1.5-2.0x faster than FlashAttention-2 in FP16, reaching up to 740 TFLOPs/s (~75% of peak) FP16, 840 TFLOPs/s (~85%) BF16, and ~1.2-1.3 PFLOPs/s in FP8.

flashcards.q: What three techniques does FlashAttention-3 use to hit its H100 numbers?
flashcards.a: Warp-specialized async overlap of Tensor Core matmuls with TMA data movement, interleaved block-wise matmul/softmax scheduling, and FP8 support with incoherent processing to control quantization error.

flashcards.q: Can GQA or MLA be added to an existing pretrained MHA checkpoint as a serving-time optimization?
flashcards.a: No -- both are architecture decisions baked in during pretraining (or continued pretraining); they cannot be retrofitted at inference time the way PagedAttention or quantization can.
